blocks.task_summary: Use the exponential model P(t)=15000e^{kt}, k<0, t≥0 to estimate the population on 1 January 2041, given an 11% decrease between 1 January 2014 (t=0) and 1 January 2022 (t=8).
method_path: Solve for k using natural logarithm: k=ln(0.89)/8≈−0.014566
Substitute t=27 into P(t)=15000e^{kt} and compute P(27)≈10100 (10122)

evidence.basis: recognition that initial population is 15000 (seen anywhere) (A1); P(0)=15000 OR 0.11×15000 OR 0.89×15000; population after 11% decrease is 15000×0.89=13350 (A1); recognizing that t=8 on 1 January 2022 (seen anywhere) (A1); substitution of their value of t for 1 January 2022 and their value of P(8) into the model (M1); 15000×0.89=15000e^{8k} OR 13350=15000e^{8k}; k=ln(0.89)/8≈−0.014566 (A1); substitution of t=2041−2014=27 and their value for k into the model (M1); P(27)=15000e^{−0.0145...×27}=10122.3…; P(27)=10100 (10122) (A1); Total [7 marks]
